summary:
ASTRA is a web-based prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions.

The project combines an interactive 3D human body explorer with a health monitoring dashboard. Users can explore different body areas, view health indicators, monitor physiological measurements such as heart rate and blood pressure, and track recorded observations through charts and visual indicators. ASTRA also includes a backend system for storing, managing, and retrieving health data.

The system addresses the challenges astronauts face in space, including altered gravity, radiation exposure, isolation, and limited access to immediate medical assistance. By organizing health information in one accessible platform, ASTRA aims to help astronauts recognize potential health concerns and make more informed decisions.

ASTRA is important for the future of human space exploration, particularly long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars. Its modular design provides a foundation for future improvements, including intelligent health assessment, automated alerts, and more advanced astronaut health support.
details:
ASTRA is a web-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to support crew members during long-duration space missions.

How It Works:
ASTRA combines an interactive 3D human body explorer with a health monitoring dashboard. Users can explore different body areas, view health indicators, and monitor physiological measurements such as heart rate and blood pressure. The system allows manual entry of health readings, stores observations, and displays measurement history through charts and visual indicators. Its backend manages health records and provides structured access to stored data.

Benefits and Intended Impact:
ASTRA aims to help astronauts monitor their physical condition, recognize potential health concerns, and access organized health information without depending entirely on immediate communication with Earth. It provides a foundation for more autonomous health monitoring during future Moon and Mars missions.

Tools and Technologies:
The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the frontend, Python and FastAPI for the backend, and SQLite for local data storage. Chart.js was used for data visualization, alongside JavaScript-based 3D visualization components. Uvicorn was used to run the backend server. Development and testing were performed on a Windows computer.

Creativity and Design Considerations:
ASTRA introduces a visual approach to astronaut health monitoring by connecting human anatomy exploration with physiological data. Its modular design considers usability, accessibility, data organization, and the unique challenges of space environments, including isolation, radiation exposure, altered gravity, and limited medical support. The prototype is designed to allow future expansion with intelligent health assessment, automated alerts, and integration with wearable health sensors.
